newsitem.title: USA: Loral to acquire AT&T's SKYNET satellite unit.
newsitem.headline: Loral to acquire AT&T's SKYNET satellite unit.

text.p: Loral Space & Communications Ltd. said Wednesday it agreed to buy AT&T Corp.'s SKYNET satellite service for $712.5 million in cash, forming one of the world's largest satellite-based businesses.
Loral, which manufactures as well as operates satellites, said the acquisition was part of its strategy to become a dominant force in providing multi-media satellite services around the world.

"The demand for satellite services is huge and growing," Loral's expansion-minded chairman and chief executive, Bernard Schwartz, said in a statement. "SKYNET will serve as a critical building block for our worldwide satellite network service strategy.
"Historically a domestic provider, SKYNET not only jump starts our U.S. capabilities, but provides us with a world-class platform for expansion into the international arena," Schwartz added.

SKYNET owns and operates four Telstar satellites that primarily distribute entertainment and educational programming to mass audiences. It also has two state-of-the-art satellite control stations and a research and development facility.
Its customers include some of the biggest content providers in the broadcast industry, including Walt Disney Co.'s ABC network, News Corp.'s Fox network, and the Public Broadcasting System.

Schwartz said the acquisition of SKYNET will complement Loral's two other strategic initiatives -- a constellation of 48 low-orbit satellites to provide worldwide telephone services and a fleet of high-flying geostationary satellites to provide a low-cost, two-way digital communications system.
"SKYNET significantly adds to Loral's ability to develop a major, truly integrated system of GEO (geostationary) and LEO (low earth orbit) satellite networks," Schwartz said.

Loral said the acquisition of SKYNET, which derives most of its revenues from noncancelable long-term contracts for telecommunications services, is expected to add about $30 million to its pre-tax earnings in 1998, SKYNET'S first full year under Loral ownership.

It added that even without a full-year's benefit from the launch of a fifth Telstar satellite, SKYNET'S 1997 revenues should exceed $145 million and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization should be $95 million.
Loral added that revenues and earnings are expected to increase dramatically as recently launched satellites and satellites currently under construction are deployed.
Loral SKYNET, as the company will be called, will also continue to serve AT&T's current satellite customers and will support other AT&T communications services.
SKYNET, which is based in Bedminster, N.J., has operations centres in Hawley, Pa., and Three Peaks, Calif., and a research and development facility in Holmdel, N.J.
Loral, which has grown over the years primarily through acquisitions, said it intends to retain all of SKYNET's employees.
The company also said it will use $500 million of debt to finance the pruchase, leaving it with about $400 million in cash after the transaction.

AT&T, which is breaking itself into three companies, said it was selling the satellite unit to concentrate on its core business. The communications giant shocked Wall Street Tuesday by saying its revenues would be substantially lower this year, primarily due to competition in the long-distance telephone business.
Loral's stock gained $1.125 to $14.375 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
AT&T, which plunged $5.625 Tuesday after its gloomy earnings forecast, slipped another 12.5 cents to $51.375, also on the NYSE.
